Running the restaurant has gotten harder. I’m distracted in the middle of a dinner rush because I’m checking my skin, or pressing on my abdomen to see if anything feels different. At the same time, there are days when I get this sudden burst of energy. I’ll stay up most of the night rearranging menus, planning expansions, talking nonstop to my husband about new ideas. I don’t feel tired at all then—almost wired—and I spend money on things for the restaurant that we probably can’t afford. Those phases come and go; sometimes I’m more focused on my body, sometimes more on these big plans, and it all sort of blurs together.
